questions.stem: In TURBT patients, which comorbidities are often present?
questions.answer: Often smokers, with comorbidities such as COPD and IHD

questions.stem: Why review a TURBT patient's previous anaesthetic charts?
What spinal block level is needed for TURBT?
What anaesthetic options are used for TURBT?
questions.answer: General anaesthesia (LMA) or spinal, with or without sedation

questions.stem: What patient position is used for TURBT?
How does blood loss behave during TURBT?
What may guide antibiotic prophylaxis for TURBT?
During TURBT, what can help with obturator spasm?
questions.answer: Muscle relaxation or an obturator nerve block

questions.stem: Why check volume status before a diuretic for bladder flushing in TURBT?
questions.answer: The patient must not be hypovolaemic

questions.stem: What bladder problem can be marked after TURBT?
In TURBT, which nerve runs next to the lateral bladder wall?
Why does irrigation raise obturator nerve risk in TURBT?
questions.answer: It distends the lateral wall, bringing it close to the nerve

questions.stem: In TURBT, what causes the obturator jerk?
questions.answer: Diathermy resection of lateral wall tumours stimulating the nerve

questions.stem: What is the main danger of an obturator jerk during TURBT?
In TURBT, when do surgeons often request anaesthetic options for obturator spasm?
questions.answer: When the surgeon works near the nerve
